subject: Three separate signals that immersive went mainstream

hero.statement: Immersive went mainstream on three fronts this week
hero.sub: Not one story, three. A studio filling venues across three continents, a Hollywood studio betting on domes, and an artist moving his life's work into the headset.

sections.statement: Wevr filled venues on three continents
sections.body: LA studio Wevr reported five location based experiences across Asia, Europe and South America reaching more than a million people this year, including The Blu: Expedition Taiwan, built with HTC VIVERSE and Taiwan's Ministry of Culture in Kaohsiung.
sections.why: Shared immersive rooms are destinations. Destinations sell tickets a headset at home never will.

sections.statement: Sony put 100 million dollars into domes
sections.body: Sony is investing 100 million dollars in Cosm, the domed theater operator, which opens a fourth venue in Detroit this September and a fifth in Cleveland after that. The wraparound dome is spreading fast.
sections.why: When a studio like Sony bankrolls domes, the format has moved from novelty to real estate.

sections.statement: A named artist moved his catalog into spatial
sections.body: A.R. Rahman launched ARR Immersive on Apple Vision Pro, bringing a decade of immersive storytelling into a spatial app. When artists of that scale port their work, brands get a lane to build inside it.
sections.why: Cultural credibility is borrowable. Partner early and you sit inside the story, not beside it.

invitation.headline: Design for the room, not the headset
invitation.body: The immersive work that travels is the work people do together. We design shared, real time experiences for brands and agencies, your name on the front, our engine underneath.
